propositions.text: The appellant family from Mexico is appealing the RPD's rejection of their refugee claim.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, his spouse XXXX XXXX XXXX and their three minor daughters, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, all citizens of Mexico, are appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) to reject their refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Mexican appellant family is appealing the RPD's refugee claim rejection.

propositions.text: They submit no new evidence and do not request a hearing before the RAD.
propositions.quote: They are not submitting any new evidence in their appeal and are not requesting that a hearing be held before the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD).

paragraphs.summary: The appellants say they submit no new evidence and do not request a hearing before the RAD.

propositions.text: The female appellant was appointed designated representative of the three minor daughters.
propositions.quote: The female appellant, XXXX XXXX XXXX, was appointed the designated representative of the three minor daughters.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the female appellant was appointed representative of the minor daughters.

propositions.text: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination that the appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the RAD confirms the determination of the RPD, namely, that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are neither "Convention refugees" under section 96 of the IRPA nor "persons in need of protection" under section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD's decision that the appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The principal appellant alleged extortion by criminals while working as a bus driver in XXXX.
propositions.quote: In the Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form) that he filed before the RPD, the principal appellant alleges that he was extorted by criminals while working as a bus driver in XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD record shows the principal appellant alleged extortion by criminals while working as a bus driver.

propositions.text: The principal appellant alleges he was beaten on XXXX XXXX, 2016, by criminals accusing him of not paying money for two weeks.
propositions.quote: He alleges that he was beaten on XXXX XXXX, 2016, by these criminals, who accused him of not having given them money for the two preceeding weeks.

propositions.text: His spouse received a fake kidnapping call on XXXX XXXX, 2016.
propositions.quote: He alleges that his spouse received a telephone call faking his kidnapping on XXXX XXXX, 2016.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD record states the appellant was beaten and his spouse received a fake kidnapping call in 2016.

propositions.text: The appellants left Mexico for Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2016, to claim refugee protection.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, 2016, the appellants left Mexico for Canada, where they claimed refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants left Mexico for Canada in 2016 to claim refugee protection, per the RPD record.

propositions.text: The female appellant and minors base their claim on the principal appellant's claim.
propositions.quote: The female appellant, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and the minor appellants are basing their claim on that of the principal appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The female appellant and minors base their claim on the principal appellant's claim, per the RPD record.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the refugee claim due to the male appellant's lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD rejected the refugee protection claim on the basis that the male appellant's allegations were not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the claim because it found the male appellant not credible.

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD erred in assessing their credibility, to be detailed later if necessary.
propositions.quote: Before the RAD, the appellants submit that the RPD erred in its assessment of their credibility, for reasons that will be detailed later in the "Analysis" section, if necessary.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD erred in assessing their credibility, to be detailed later.

propositions.text: The appellants ask the RAD to set aside the RPD decision and grant protection or refer for re-determination.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the appellants are asking the RAD to set aside the determination of the RPD and grant them refugee protection, or, alternitavely, to refer the matter to the RPD for re-determination.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants ask the RAD to set aside the RPD decision and grant protection or refer for re-determination.

propositions.text: The RAD reviews RPD decisions for correctness but defers on credibility findings where RPD has a meaningful advantage.
propositions.quote: The RAD's role is to review RPD decisions using the correctness standard of review after conducting its own analysis of the record in order to determine whether the RPD erred, as submitted by the appellant. The exception to this rule concerns the RPD's findings in the assessment of the credibility of or the weight to be given to the oral evidence it hears, in cases where it enjoys a meaningful advantage.

propositions.text: Canada v. Huruglica establishes RAD owes deference to RPD credibility findings when RPD has meaningful advantage.
propositions.quote: The RAD then owes a measure of deference to the RPD's findings (Canada v. Huruglica, F.C.A., No. A-470-14).

propositions.text: The court will provide reasons if it finds the RPD had a meaningful advantage.
propositions.quote: In my analysis, I will provide reasons if I find that the RPD had a meaningful advantage.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains RAD reviews RPD decisions for correctness but defers on credibility findings if RPD has meaningful advantage.

propositions.text: The issue is whether the RPD erred in assessing the appellants' credibility.
propositions.quote: The issue in this case is whether the RPD erred in its assessment of the appellants' credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the issue is whether the RPD erred in assessing credibility.

propositions.text: The court finds the RPD did not err in its credibility assessment for reasons to follow.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the answer to this question is no, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD did not err in credibility assessment, reasons to follow.

propositions.text: The RPD based its decision partly on the principal appellant's vague testimony about his work.
propositions.quote: The RPD based its decision on the following elements: A. The principal appellant's testimony about his work was vague.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the principal appellant's testimony about his work was vague.

propositions.text: The principal appellant could not explain salary, hours, schedule, and claimed a special bus driver's licence inconsistent with evidence.
propositions.quote: He was unable to explain simple elements such as his salary, his hours and who determined his schedule. Furthermore, he testified that he had a special driver's licence authorizing him to drive a bus, while the licence he filed in evidence indicates that he can only drive private vehicles.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant could not explain work details and his licence evidence contradicted his claim.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the RPD that the male appellant's testimony was vague about his bus driver job details.
propositions.quote: Listening to the recording of the hearing before the RPD, I come to the same conclusion as the latter on this subject. The male appellant's testimony was vague in that he was unable to explain the conditions of his alleged job as a bus driver, such as the name of his employer, his co-workers, his hours, his salary, and who or what determines his schedule.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that the appellant's testimony about his job was vague.

propositions.text: The court finds the appellant's explanation that he was 'mixed up' about his licence is unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I also find that, contrary to his testimony, his driver's licence indicates that he can only drive private vehicles. The principal claimant stated that he was [translation] "mixed up." In my opinion, this explanation is not reasonable in the context of this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant's explanation about his licence is unreasonable.

propositions.text: The appellant lacks a bus driver's licence and did not file official documents proving his job since 2003.
propositions.quote: Not only does the male appellant not have the driver's licence authorizing him to drive a bus, but he also did not file any other official document that could establish his job as a bus driver, which he alleges to have had since 2003.

propositions.text: The attestation filed is a letter without letterhead from an unknown source and insufficient to support his allegations.
propositions.quote: The attestation filed as Exhibit D-3 (page 268 of the RPD record) is just a letter, without letterhead, from a source unknown to the panel, and it is therefore insufficient to support the male appellant's allegations, given his vague and contradictory testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant lacks a bus licence and official proof; the attestation is insufficient and from an unknown source.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the RPD that it is implausible the appellant drove a bus for 13 years without the required licence or employer/insurance requiring it.
propositions.quote: As the RPD concluded, I am of the opinion that it is implausible that the male appellant could have driven a bus without the required licence and that neither his employer nor his insurance company ever required him to obtain it.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that it is implausible the appellant drove a bus 13 years without a licence or employer requiring it.

propositions.text: It is unlikely the male appellant never had to show his licence to authorities during 13 years.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that it is unlikely that the male appellant has never had to show his licence to authorities during these 13 years.

propositions.text: It is not credible that the male appellant never spoke to his employer about his alleged problems or asked to change his schedule.
propositions.quote: It is not credible that the male appellant never spoke to his employer about his alleged problems and never asked to change his schedule.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD finds it unlikely the male appellant never showed his licence to authorities and not credible he never spoke to his employer about problems or schedule.

propositions.text: The male appellant's answer 'No, why?' undermines his credibility about speaking to his employer.
propositions.quote: this response already undermines the male appellant's credibility: it seems logical to me to discuss the extortion problem with his employer

propositions.text: The male appellant's explanation that no other schedule exists is neither logical nor reasonable.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, this explanation is neither logical nor reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD finds the male appellant's denial of speaking to employer and his explanation about schedule illogical and undermining credibility.

propositions.text: The letter from a co-worker adds confusion to the male appellant's testimony.
propositions.quote: this letter adds to the confusion of the male appellant's testimony.

propositions.text: The letter is allegedly from a co-worker though the appellant said he had only one co-worker whose name he does not know.
propositions.quote: The letter is allegedly from a co-worker, even though the male appellant testified that he had only one co-worker whose name he does not know

propositions.text: The letter's author seems familiar with appellant's problems though appellant said he never spoke about them.
propositions.quote: the author of this letter seems familiar with the male appellant's problems, even though he testified that he never spoke about them

propositions.text: The letter mentions several colleagues and refers to 'taxi base', not buses.
propositions.quote: the letter seems to mention several colleagues (the author uses "we") and refers to the "taxi base," not buses

propositions.text: The letter's author filed a driver's licence showing authorization to drive buses, unlike the male appellant's licence.
propositions.quote: The author also filed a copy of his driver's licence in evidence, which indicates that he is authorized to drive buses, contrary to the male appellant's licence.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD finds the co-worker's letter inconsistent with appellant's testimony and confusing, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: The male appellant does not know his insurance company name.
propositions.quote: the fact that he does not know the name of his insurance company

propositions.text: The attackers allegedly knew 'all about him' but did not know his name yet found his contact info.
propositions.quote: he alleges that his attackers knew "all about him," yet they did not know his name and still allegedly found his personal contact information

propositions.text: He testified meeting attackers three times but changed to six times when confronted with BOC Form.
propositions.quote: he testified that he met his attackers three times before changing his answer to six times when confronted with his BOC Form

propositions.text: He alleged police were accomplices without reasonable explanation.
propositions.quote: he alleged that the police were accomplices to the criminals without a reasonable explanation for the basis of this statement

paragraphs.summary: The RPD identifies several elements undermining the male appellant's credibility including inconsistencies and unsupported allegations.

propositions.text: Elements alone are not fatal but together with prior elements undermine appellant's central allegations.
propositions.quote: these elements considered seperately are not fatal to the claim; however, when considered together with elements A through D mentioned above, I find that there is sufficient evidence to undermine the credibility of the appellant's central allegations

paragraphs.summary: The RPD finds combined credibility issues sufficient to undermine appellant's central allegations.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by not considering the Mexican context of the alleged events.
propositions.quote: the appellants submit that the RPD erred by not considering the Mexican context in which the alleged events happened

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD erred by ignoring the Mexican context of events.

propositions.text: The Mexican context cannot explain contradictions and inconsistencies in appellant's testimony.
propositions.quote: this context cannot, however, explain the contradictions and inconsistencies noted

propositions.text: The male appellant did not explain how Mexican context justifies contradictions or vague testimony.
propositions.quote: The male appellant did not explain at the hearing or in his appeal memorandum how the Mexican context could justify the contradictions, inconsistencies, and vague and imprecise nature of his testimony

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Mexican context does not explain contradictions or vague testimony and appellant gave no explanation.

propositions.text: Appellants failed to show RPD errors warranting RAD intervention.
propositions.quote: I find that the appellants failed to establish that the RPD committed errors warranting the RAD's intervention

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes appellants failed to show RPD errors justifying RAD intervention.

propositions.text: The RPD's determination that appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection is confirmed.
propositions.quote: I confirm the determination of the RPD, namely, that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are neither "Convention refugees" under section 96 of the IRPA nor "persons in need of protection" withing the meaning of section 97 of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD's determination appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
